newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher with southern heat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher with southern heat.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Monday as temperatures in the South were forecast to top 100 degrees F over the next couple of days, industry sources said.
August over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.15 to $2.16 after settling to the upside Friday at $2.139 per million British thermal units.

"You're probably going to get another pop...I think it will probably settle around $2.16-2.165," one trader said, noting the market's strength could be attributed to strong technicals, hot and humid weather and nuclear snags.
Technically, traders said August support was at $2.14 and along the up trendline at $2.105. Next support was seen at the recent $2.08 low. Trendline resistance was seen at $2.18, $2.22 and $2.27.
With little activity in the cash market and the upcoming Independence Day holiday, most traders expected trading to be light.

In Friday's cash, Gulf Coast gas prices firmed slightly to the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes were steady to off slightly at about $2. New York city gate gas for July was quoted in the mid-$2.40s, up five cents on the day.

Temperatures across the South and Northeast were expected to remain several degrees above normal before returning to near-normal in Texas and the southern plains by midweek, according to Weather Services Corp.
Separately, the 1,250 megawatt South Texas 1 nuclear unit was reduced to about 69 percent power over the weekend for repairs, while Entergy Corp's 836 MW Arkansas 1 unit was cut to 55 percent.
